nextChange: Audit and recommend principles/checks only; no implementation change requested.

sources.summary: Owner-approved single-reader journey and first-version exclusions.
Local Node, JSON persistence and queue/public-operation boundary.
Read articles remain in the queue; mark read preserves title and address.
Three documents, no executable application or check configuration.

findings.problem: No executable acceptance protection for the approved journey.
findings.principle: Keep article identity and queue membership stable.
findings.consequence: A mark-read implementation could discard title/address or remove read articles.
findings.fix: Add public-operation and real-presentation acceptance tests: save two distinct articles, list, mark one read, list again and restart/reload JSON. Assert exact title/address preservation, read article remains, and second article is unchanged.
findings.verification: Run node --test with temporary storage plus a real presentation smoke flow. Expectations come from VISION.md:5, DESIGN.md:6 and glossary.md:4-5.

findings.problem: The documented presentation/storage boundary has no executable or review protection.
findings.principle: Queue owns mutations; presentation uses only public operations.
findings.consequence: Direct storage writes can bypass mark-read invariants.
findings.fix: At first implementation, keep presentation, queue operations and JSON adapter responsibilities explicit. Use import-graph review now; add a native semantic import restriction only if the selected tool supports it. Avoid regex rules.
findings.verification: Review resolved imports and storage writes; prove allowed public import passes and deliberate direct-storage import fails if automating.

findings.problem: Persistence failure behaviour has no implementation or protection.
findings.principle: Proposed: failed persistence must not silently discard saved articles.
findings.consequence: Malformed JSON or a failed write could erase the reader’s queue.
findings.fix: Handle an absent file as an empty queue; report malformed JSON without overwriting it. Serialize mutations and write via temporary file/replacement appropriate to the supported platform; do not report success before persistence completes.
findings.verification: Real temporary-file checks: restart round trip, malformed JSON preserved byte-for-byte, failed-write error surfaced and prior valid data retained. Do not claim universal crash durability from these tests.

findings.problem: There is no reproducible setup or maintained check command.
findings.principle: Proposed: a clean checkout must reproduce setup and journey checks.
findings.consequence: Later contributors could get a green run with no tests or inconsistent tools.
findings.fix: When implementation lands, document supported Node/setup/start/check commands, make tests actually discoverable, and adopt one formatter/linter if useful. Keep review rules in DESIGN.md, config as mechanical authority. Add JS checkJs or TS noEmit only if that language setup is selected; CI is a separate selection.
findings.verification: Clean-checkout setup and start smoke test; node --test must execute the required cases, formatter/lint and applicable type checks pass. No host version is silently adopted as project pin.

findings.problem: No code exists to assess first-version scope compliance.
findings.principle: Keep the local single-reader scope and purposeful dependencies.
findings.consequence: Accounts, sharing or recommendations would expand the approved first version.
findings.fix: Review each proposed capability/dependency against save, list, mark-read and local JSON persistence. Preserve current vision/design/glossary as authority; do not generate a replacement vision or duplicate standards.
findings.verification: Human review maps each capability to VISION.md:4-6 and DESIGN.md:3-5. This is judgement, not a static violation.

limitations: Research ran in main thread: three small files made delegation wasteful.
